It is our opinion that the Budget as prepared for 'Your consideration
is an ample one, one that will be prudentl y used by conscientious and
clear thinking members of this great Masonic Fraternit y. Wherev er savings can be made, they will, as in past years be made.
Howeve r the income this year from the present $2 per capita tax is
not sufficient to cover our total budgeted expenses. In order to come
close to a balanced budget, we have necessarily increased our estimated
revenue by $23,000, equivalent to 10 cents per capita.
We accordingly offer the following resolution:

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

NOTE: By direction of the Grand Master, the following is included as
a part of the record of these Proceedings:

RESOLUTION
WHEREAS, Paul August Pflueger, a member of a pioneer San
Francisco family, has devoted his life in the service of city, state and
country through partidpation in many civic and community activities,
and
WHEREAS, he has been by precept and example a leader in his
beloved Masonic Fraternity and particularly Amity-Seal Rock Lodge
No. 370 in which he was raised on February 25, 1916, and served as its
Master in 1924, and
WHEREAS, as he was appointed the first Assistant Grand Treasurer of the Grand Lodge of Free and Accepted Masons of the State of
California in 1948 on the recommendation of Grand Treasurer Francis
V. Keesling who stated, "It is the intent that the appointment of such
officer should be based on successful investment experience," and
WHEREAS, time has demonstrated that the recommendation of
Grand Treasurer Keesling was sound and wise, and
WHEREAS, in 1964 Brother Pflueger was appointed and subsequenty elected Grand Treasurer of this Grand Lodge, and
WHEREAS, he served as Chairman of the Investment Committee
of Grand Lodge and its entities since he became Assistant Grand Treasurer, and
WHEREAS, it was his knowledge and experience that prompted
the report on the "Prudent Man Rule" to Grand Lodge, which report
was subsequently adopted as the guide for future investments of Grand
Lodge, its entities, and all constituent Lodges,
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that, by direction of
the Grand Master, Most Worshipful Herbert A. Huebner, and the
Elective Officers, the Grand Lodge of Free and Accepted Masons of
California express to Very Worshipful Paul A. Pflueger in recognition
of his voluntary retirement from the office of Grand Treasurer its highest
praise, appreciation and grateful thanks for the time, effort and experience he has so unselfishly and generously contributed for the benefit of
all Masons of this Jurisdiction, and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Grand Secretary shall
cause this expression of appreciation to be properly inscribed for presentation to Brother Pflueger as a symbol of the respect and admiration held
for him by Masons whithersoever dispersed.

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

341

INSTALLATION OF OFFICERS
Most Worshipful Ellsworth Meyer, Past Grand Master, acted as
Master of Ceremonies and the ofBcers, elected and appointed, were
installed by the retiring Grand Master in accordance with the Ritual.
The Grand Master's lapel pin was transferred from the retiring to
the newly installed Grand Master. The Arthur S. Crites lapel pins were
then exchanged by the other chair ofBcers.
Very Worshipful H. Douglas Lemons explained that following his
appointment to that ofBce he had been presented the Grand Lecturer's
lapel pin by the widow of Harold N. Richards.
In the absence of Reverend Hornaday, Grand Master Huebner
presented the pin of the Grand Chaplain to Very Reverend Roland R.
Bach.
The retiring Grand Master was presented with a gift for his wife,
Majorie, on behalf of the members of Grand Lodge, and a Past Grand
Master Pin by Most Worshipful Eugene S. Hopp. He was then invested
with the apron of his new designation by Worshipful Alfred W. Odle
and presented a Past Grand Master Certificate by Most Worshipful
Myron E. Smith. Most Worshipful Chester R. MacPhee expressed
his sincere appreciation for these several presentations.
Our newly installed Grand Master, Most Worshipful Herbert A.
Huebner, acknowledged the presence of members of his Lodge, Wilshire No. 445, who were in attendance for his installation as an indication of their fraternal love and respect. He also expressed his gratitude
and sense of humility for having been called upon by members of the
fraternity to servt: in this high ofBce of Freemasonry.
At 12:35 P.M., all business being completed, Gt-and Lodge closed
in duefonn.

NOTE A - Basis of Accounting
The financial statements are presented on a modified cash
basis of accounting, Generally, revenues are recorded at the time of
receipt and expenses ar~ accrued at year end,
NOTE B - Purpose of Foundation
The California Masonic Foundation was established on March 5,

1969, primarily for charitable, educational and scientific purposes.
Income from these funds has been used for student scholarships.

The California Ma.sonic Foundation has recorded the Masonic
clubhouse at the University of California at Los Angeles on its books
at a value of one dollar. The Foundation is currently attempting to

to ~urchase the property, The option was not exercised and a deposit
of ,25,000 was forfeited to the Foundation,
NOTE D - Other Assets

at a nominal value of on~ dollar. The lease expires during July 1985
or, if oil or gas is found, during July 2064.
